Planning to write a temporary probe script to test fixer change detection.

The probe will run the fix pipeline twice on three fixtures: no-op, single reorder, and nested reorder. It will compare raw versus printed output, check print-to-print stability between passes, and measure stability across two fix runs.

The probe will verify idempotency by re-fixing the already-fixed output. Print-to-print comparison correctly flags reordering while ignoring no-op fixtures. Raw-versus-printed detection risks false positives on no-op cases where early returns bypass the fix. The script will use bun to import directly from the codebase.

import ts from &#39;typescript&#39;;
import { readFileSync } from &#39;fs&#39;;
import { fixParsedFile } from &#39;./src/fixer.ts&#39;;
import { analyzeParsedFile } from &#39;./src/analyzer.ts&#39;;
import { FileService } from &#39;./src/services/FileService.ts&#39;;

const printer = ts.createPrinter({ newLine: ts.NewLineKind.LineFeed });

function printSource(content: string, path: string): string {
  const sf = ts.createSourceFile(path, content, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true);
  return printer.printFile(sf);
}

function probe(label: string, path: string) {
  const raw = readFileSync(path, &#39;utf8&#39;);
  const service = new FileService();
  const parsed = service.parseContent(raw, path);
  const analysis = analyzeParsedFile(parsed);

  // Pass 1: fix from raw
  const pass1 = fixParsedFile({ content: raw, filePath: path, analysisResult: analysis });
  const printRaw = printSource(raw, path);
  const printPass1 = printSource(pass1.fixedContent, path);

  // Pass 2: fix from pass1 output (re-analyze)
  const parsed2 = service.parseContent(pass1.fixedContent, path);
  const analysis2 = analyzeParsedFile(parsed2);
  const pass2 = fixParsedFile({ content: pass1.fixedContent, filePath: path, analysisResult: analysis2 });
  const printPass2 = printSource(pass2.fixedContent, path);

  // Also: force-reorder print path without early-return gate (simulate reorder always)
  // by comparing print identity strategies on pass1 content
  const rawVsFixed = raw !== pass1.fixedContent;
  const printToPrintChange = printRaw !== printPass1;
  const printPassStable = printPass1 === printPass2;
  const fixedContentStable = pass1.fixedContent === pass2.fixedContent;
  const pass1FixedFlag = pass1.fixed;
  const pass2FixedFlag = pass2.fixed;

  // normalized: collapse whitespace
  const norm = (s: string) =&gt; s.replace(/\r\n/g, &#39;\n&#39;).replace(/[ \t]+/g, &#39; &#39;).replace(/\n+/g, &#39;\n&#39;).trim();
  const normChange = norm(printRaw) !== norm(printPass1);
  const normStable = norm(printPass1) === norm(printPass2);

  console.log(JSON.stringify({
    label,
    path,
    violations: analysis.violations.length,
    nestedViolations: analysis.nestedFunctionViolations.length,
    pass1: { fixed: pass1FixedFlag, reordered: pass1.reordered, contentLen: pass1.fixedContent.length },
    pass2: { fixed: pass2FixedFlag, reordered: pass2.reordered, contentLen: pass2.fixedContent.length },
    strategies: {
      rawInequality_wouldDetectChange: rawVsFixed,
      printToPrint_wouldDetectChange: printToPrintChange,
      normalizedPrint_wouldDetectChange: normChange,
      printPass1_eq_printPass2: printPassStable,
      fixedContent_eq_acrossPasses: fixedContentStable,
      normPassStable: normStable,
    },
    lengths: { raw: raw.length, printRaw: printRaw.length, printPass1: printPass1.length, printPass2: printPass2.length },
    // show if raw!==print even when no structural change (false positive risk)
    raw_vs_printRaw: raw !== printRaw,
  }, null, 2));
}

probe(&#39;no-op&#39;, &#39;fixtures/test-correct.ts&#39;);
probe(&#39;single-reorder&#39;, &#39;fixtures/test-violations.ts&#39;);
probe(&#39;nested-reorder&#39;, &#39;fixtures/test-nested-violation.ts&#39;);

```bash
bun -e "
import ts from 'typescript';
import { readFileSync } from 'fs';
import { fixParsedFile } from './src/fixer.ts';
import { analyzeParsedFile } from './src/analyzer.ts';
import { FileService } from './src/services/FileService.ts';

const printer = ts.createPrinter({ newLine: ts.NewLineKind.LineFeed });

function printSource(content: string, path: string): string {
  const sf = ts.createSourceFile(path, content, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true);
  return printer.printFile(sf);
}

function probe(label: string, path: string) {
  const raw = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
  const service = new FileService();
  const parsed = service.parseContent(raw, path);
  const analysis = analyzeParsedFile(parsed);

  // Pass 1: fix from raw
  const pass1 = fixParsedFile({ content: raw, filePath: path, analysisResult: analysis });
  const printRaw = printSource(raw, path);
  const printPass1 = printSource(pass1.fixedContent, path);

  // Pass 2: fix from pass1 output (re-analyze)
  const parsed2 = service.parseContent(pass1.fixedContent, path);
  const analysis2 = analyzeParsedFile(parsed2);
  const pass2 = fixParsedFile({ content: pass1.fixedContent, filePath: path, analysisResult: analysis2 });
  const printPass2 = printSource(pass2.fixedContent, path);

  // Also: force-reorder print path without early-return gate (simulate reorder always)
  // by comparing print identity strategies on pass1 content
  const rawVsFixed = raw !== pass1.fixedContent;
  const printToPrintChange = printRaw !== printPass1;
  const printPassStable = printPass1 === printPass2;
  const fixedContentStable = pass1.fixedContent === pass2.fixedContent;
  const pass1FixedFlag = pass1.fixed;
  const pass2FixedFlag = pass2.fixed;

  // normalized: collapse whitespace
  const norm = (s: string) => s.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/[ \t]+/g, ' ').replace(/\n+/g, '\n').trim();
  const normChange = norm(printRaw) !== norm(printPass1);
  const normStable = norm(printPass1) === norm(printPass2);

  console.log(JSON.stringify({
    label,
    path,
    violations: analysis.violations.length,
    nestedViolations: analysis.nestedFunctionViolations.length,
    pass1: { fixed: pass1FixedFlag, reordered: pass1.reordered, contentLen: pass1.fixedContent.length },
    pass2: { fixed: pass2FixedFlag, reordered: pass2.reordered, contentLen: pass2.fixedContent.length },
    strategies: {
      rawInequality_wouldDetectChange: rawVsFixed,
      printToPrint_wouldDetectChange: printToPrintChange,
      normalizedPrint_wouldDetectChange: normChange,
      printPass1_eq_printPass2: printPassStable,
      fixedContent_eq_acrossPasses: fixedContentStable,
      normPassStable: normStable,
    },
    lengths: { raw: raw.length, printRaw: printRaw.length, printPass1: printPass1.length, printPass2: printPass2.length },
    // show if raw!==print even when no structural change (false positive risk)
    raw_vs_printRaw: raw !== printRaw,
  }, null, 2));
}

probe('no-op', 'fixtures/test-correct.ts');
probe('single-reorder', 'fixtures/test-violations.ts');
probe('nested-reorder', 'fixtures/test-nested-violation.ts');
"
```

const printer = ts.createPrinter({ newLine: ts.NewLineKind.LineFeed });

function forcePrintFix(content: string, path: string): string {
  const sf = ts.createSourceFile(path, content, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true);
  const deps = buildDependencyGraph(categorizeNodes(sf).functions, sf).dependencies;
  let nsf = applyTopLevelReorder(sf, deps);
  nsf = transformNestedBlocks(nsf);
  return printer.printFile(nsf);
}

function printOnly(content: string, path: string): string {
  return printer.printFile(ts.createSourceFile(path, content, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true));
}

const fixtures = [
  [&#39;no-op&#39;, &#39;fixtures/test-correct.ts&#39;],
  [&#39;single-reorder&#39;, &#39;fixtures/test-violations.ts&#39;],
  [&#39;nested-reorder&#39;, &#39;fixtures/test-nested-violation.ts&#39;],
];

for (const [label, path] of fixtures) {
  const raw = readFileSync(path, &#39;utf8&#39;);
  const service = new FileService();
  const analysis = analyzeParsedFile(service.parseContent(raw, path));

  // Bypass early-return: always run printer path
  const printed1 = forcePrintFix(raw, path);
  const printed2 = forcePrintFix(printed1, path); // second pass on printed output
  const printed3 = forcePrintFix(printed2, path);

  const printRaw = printOnly(raw, path);

  console.log(JSON.stringify({
    label,
    viol: analysis.violations.length,
    nested: analysis.nestedFunctionViolations.length,
    // false-positive risk of current raw!==printed
    raw_ne_printed1: raw !== printed1,
    // print-to-print strategies
    printRaw_ne_printed1: printRaw !== printed1,
    printed1_eq_printed2: printed1 === printed2,
    printed2_eq_printed3: printed2 === printed3,
    // after first print, second pass is identity
    printed1_eq_printOnly_of_printed1: printed1 === printOnly(printed1, path),
  }, null, 2));
}

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The root cause appears to be `applyTopLevelReorder` ping-ponging between two valid topological orderings of independent components. This causes unnecessary reordering even when the file is already correct.

Print-to-print stability holds under the real fixParsedFile path. Printer output is fully deterministic. Raw source inequality is a false positive caused by whitespace normalization. The no-op instability comes from topological sorting of independent components, not from printer nondeterminism.

Replacing `fixedContent !== content` with a print-to-print comparison would still fail for no-op cases. The current early-return path preserves original content when violations are zero, but the reorder-and-print path may still shuffle independent components and alter output. The spike must therefore compare the printed result against the original source rather than relying on the transformed content alone.

The post-mortem explicitly warns against comparing printer output directly against raw source text. The recommended print-to-print check compares the original untransformed AST against the transformed AST. This detects structural print differences while avoiding whitespace normalization false positives.

The concrete implementation compares `print(parse(raw))` against the already-printed `fixedContent`. The first probe confirms no-op stays stable, while single-reorder and nested reorder fixtures trigger detection on the first pass. Force-print paths remain fully deterministic.

The chosen strategy is print-to-print. The TypeScript printer is fully deterministic, so `print(x) === print(parse(print(x)))` holds. Normalized print is unnecessary because raw source inequality always produces false positives. AST hashing is more complex and unnecessary given printer determinism. Topological ordering oscillation is a separate concern for the 5x2.10 implementation.

Removing the early-return gate would expose topological oscillation to no-op files. Even a true no-op reorder shuffles independent components during transform, so the printed output differs from the original. The 5x2.10 `hasChanges` check must therefore compare the printed original against the printed transformed result. Printer determinism remains the key safeguard.

The real fix path stabilizes because the first pass fixes violations and the second pass finds zero violations, triggering the early return. To prevent topological oscillation on no-op files, the transform must either gate on violations or act as an identity when the order is already correct. Pure printer determinism should be verified by printing the same SourceFile twice and by re-parsing and re-printing the output.
</details></think>

## Spike findings: print-to-print stability

Fixtures: no-op=`fixtures/test-correct.ts`, single=`fixtures/test-violations.ts`, nested=`fixtures/test-nested-violation.ts`.

### AC1 — fix twice (real `fixParsedFile` + violation gate)

| fixture | pass1 fixed | pass2 fixed | content stable | print-to-print stable | print detects change | raw detects change | raw!==print(raw) |
|---------|-------------|-------------|----------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------|
| no-op | false | false | yes | yes | no | no | YES (false-pos risk) |
| single-reorder | true | false | yes | yes | yes | yes | YES |
| nested-reorder | true | false | yes | yes | yes | yes | YES |

### Pure TS printer (no transform)
- same SourceFile printed twice: identical
- print→parse→print round-trip: identical on all 3 fixtures
- Conclusion: **printer is deterministic**

### Caveat (out of scope for detection, note for implementer)
Force-running `applyTopLevelReorder` without violation gate oscillates on no-op/single (topo non-uniqueness across independent components). Nested-only transform is stable. Keep violation gate or make reorder identity when order already correct — detection strategy alone does not fix oscillation.

### Recommendation for stepdown-5x2.10
**Chosen strategy: print-to-print**
- Compare `print(parse(original))` vs fixed printed output (or print(original SF) vs print(transformed SF))
- Reject raw `!==` (always false-positive on whitespace)
- Normalized print / AST hash unnecessary given printer determinism

### Chosen change-detection strategy: print-to-print
- Replace `fixedContent !== content` (raw) with `print(parse(original)) !== fixedContent` (fixed already printed) OR compare print(original SF) vs print(transformed SF)
- Do NOT use raw source inequality (printer always normalizes whitespace → false positives)
- Normalized print / AST hash not needed: TS printer deterministic on probed fixtures

### Implement notes:
- Keep violation early-return OR ensure transform is identity when no reorder needed (topo can oscillate if always force-reorder)
- Fixtures for tests: test-correct (no-op), test-violations (single), test-nested-violation (nested)

## Spike result

**Strategy for 5x2.10: print-to-print** (not normalized print / AST hash)

| Fixture | Fix×2 content stable | Print-to-print stable | Detects real change | `raw !== print(raw)` |
|---------|----------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|----------------------|
| no-op (`test-correct`) | yes | yes | no (correct) | yes — false-pos risk |
| single (`test-violations`) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| nested (`test-nested-violation`) | yes | yes | yes | yes |

Pure TS printer: deterministic (same SF twice + print→parse→print). Raw inequality always false-positives on whitespace.

Caveat (implementer note): force-running `applyTopLevelReorder` without the violation gate can oscillate (topo non-uniqueness). Keep gate or make transform identity when already ordered.
